modern: When you want to cheer yourself, think of the virtues of those who live with you; for instance, the energy of one, and the modesty of another, and the generosity of a third, and some other good quality of a fourth. For nothing delights so much as the examples of the virtues, when they are shown in the characters of those who live with us and present themselves in abundance, as far as possible. So we must keep them before us.
original: When thou wishest to delight thyself, think of the virtues of those who live with thee; for instance, the activity of one, and the modesty of another, and the liberality of a third, and some other good quality of a fourth. For nothing delights so much as the examples of the virtues, when they are exhibited in the morals of those who live with us and present themselves in abundance, as far as is possible. Wherefore we must keep them before us.

explained.summary: When you need cheering up, think about the good qualities of the people around you: one person’s energy, another’s modesty, another’s generosity. Nothing lifts the spirits like seeing virtues living in the people you share your days with, so keep those examples close at hand.
explained.today: On a grim day, try listing what you admire in the people near you: the colleague who always makes the tea, the friend who never gossips, the partner who stays patient with the kids. It’s a better pick-me-up than another scroll through your phone.
